survived.claim: Reference metabolite structures are released only as hashes and the procedure that assembled the 22,136 annotated pairs from the four sources is nowhere described, so no third party can rebuild the evaluation set or recompute four of the five matching criteria.
survived.evidence: Still current in both documents. §7: "The deposited pools hold corpus substrate structures, tautomer-canonical hashes of the annotated metabolites, and candidate structures produced by this work." SI §S1: "The annotated metabolites appear only as tautomer-canonical InChIKeys, which are hashes and do not carry the structures. The deposit is therefore a list of corpus substrates, hashes of their annotations, and our own predictions." The entire account of assembly is the sentence "The annotated substrate--metabolite pairs are assembled from four sources: ChEMBL, DrugBank, MetXBioDB and the GLORYx reference set" plus the version list; no queries, fields, filters, standardisation, de-duplication, conflict rules, per-source counts, or splitting algorithm/seed appear anywhere in §2.1, SI §S1 or elsewhere. This contradicts §1: "the artifacts sufficient to recompute any cell are released" -- a hash supports only the tautomer key, not canonical SMILES, full InChIKey, first-block InChIKey or Tanimoto=1, i.e. four of the five criteria of Table S2 and four of the five rows of Table S4.
survived.fix: Add an SI subsection giving the per-source extraction and merge procedure (queries/fields, inclusion filters, structure standardisation, cross-source de-duplication and conflict resolution, per-source counts) and the splitting algorithm and seed, sufficient to regenerate the triple files against the pinned digests; and deposit reference structures for at least the 1,170-substrate evaluated test set and the 291-substrate comparison set, naming per source any that may not be redistributed.

survived.claim: Whether the trained checkpoint every GRAIL number comes from is released is never stated, and it is absent from the enumerated release, while the paper excludes a comparator from the evaluation for exactly that omission.
survived.evidence: The word "checkpoint" occurs four times in the manuscript and once in the SI, never in §7. §7 enumerates: "Source code, the split manifest, the frozen per-substrate predictions of every comparator, the evaluation harness, the provenance sweep and the preregistration with every hypothesis and its outcome are at github.com/doctawho42/GRAIL" -- no weights. Against §3.9, "Every recall figure in this paper comes from one trained checkpoint", and §4.3, "Of 4 such systems, one releases training code without a checkpoint", expanded in SI §S14: "LAGOM releases training code under Apache-2.0 but no fine-tuned checkpoint, so comparing would mean comparing against our own reimplementation." The revision that added Table S3 and itemised the curated bank did not touch §7.
survived.fix: Add one sentence to §7 stating whether the deployed generator and filter checkpoints and the 7,581-template bank are released, and release them; if a checkpoint is withheld, say so, say what it costs a reproducer, and qualify the §4.3 / S14 criticism of LAGOM so the same bar is applied to both.

survived.claim: The Data Availability Statement asserts blanket public availability and then, in the same paragraph, states the two largest pinned artifacts are undeposited and leaves whether they may be released at all as an unresolved bracketed placeholder.
survived.evidence: Unchanged in the current PDF. §7 opens "The data and software underlying this article are publicly available." Two sentences later: "The train and validation candidate pools are prepared for deposit at [ZENODO DOI, minted on publishing the deposit], held until the licence position is settled", and then "Whether they may be redistributed, and under which licence, is [CORPUS LICENCE: whether the derived corpus and the candidate pools may be redistributed, given DrugBank's terms]". §7 itself identifies these as "Two pinned artifacts ... too large to commit". SI §S15 confirms the deposit cannot proceed: "The upload is held until the licence position above is settled, and the tool refuses to run without one". The Supporting Information Available paragraph also still points at "[ZENODO DOI, minted on publishing the deposit] and from the publisher", and a third bracket now appears in SI §S5 ("[CURATED RULES: ...]").
survived.fix: Settle the licence question before resubmission and replace all three brackets with determinations; state in the indicative what is available now (code, harness, register, frozen comparator predictions) and what is withheld and why; point Supporting Information Available at the ACS-hosted SI rather than at an unminted Zenodo DOI.

survived.claim: Three of the six "confirmed" registered predictions are adjudicated on the point estimate although their own intervals straddle the registered threshold, so the data establish only that the effect exceeds zero.
survived.evidence: Current text, unchanged: P1 "threshold of +0.05 ... +0.0733, 95% CI [+0.0477, +0.102]" (§2.4); P2 "a threshold of +0.015; measured +0.026, 95% CI [+0.0033, +0.0469]" (§2.5); P5 "at a registered +0.02 ... Measured +0.0286, 95% CI [+0.0085, +0.0502]" (§3.8). Each lower bound sits below its threshold. §3.7 nonetheless reports "six confirmed and three failed", and Table 4's six passes are P1-P5 and P9. The paper applies the opposite standard elsewhere -- Table S4 caption: "Every cell is read from the interval and never from the point estimate." The revision made P1 worse, not better: §2.3 now reports the deployed-pool contrast as "+0.0519, 95% CI [+0.0246, +0.0812]", which straddles +0.05 by more.
survived.fix: Adjudicate each registered prediction by comparing its interval to its threshold, as Table S4 already does for the comparison: mark P1, P2 and P5 unresolved and restate §3.7's tally; or state explicitly that the registered falsification condition was written on the point estimate and give the interval verdict alongside it.

survived.claim: The 45 comparison verdicts are each read from a per-cell nominal 95% interval with no multiplicity control anywhere, and the abstract's significance claims are cells selected from that grid.
survived.evidence: Table S4 is 5 criteria x 9 budgets = 45 verdicts, and the revision added 54 more intervals in Table S3 ("Every difference between a GRAIL arm and a comparator on the comparison set, in micro recall, with its paired bootstrap 95% interval ... The estimator is Equation 6 at B = 10 000 resamples, seed 0"). Neither caption, nor §2.8 ("A claim that the system leads is made for a cell only where that cell's interval excludes zero"), states that these are per-comparison, unadjusted intervals; the only multiplicity control in either document is in a different analysis, SI §S11 ("none survives a Holm correction"). The abstract's "GRAIL ahead at k = 30 and k = 50, each with the paired interval excluding zero" rests at k=30 on the single narrowest cell in Table S3, +.038 [+.005, +.072], which SI §S3 itself flags: "The exhaustive mode's lead over MetaTox at k = 30 excludes zero by little."
survived.fix: One sentence in §2.8 stating that every interval in Table S3, Table S4 and Figure 1 is a per-comparison 95% interval with no family-wise adjustment, and a note that the k=30 lead is the one abstract cell that would not survive one.

survived.claim: The training-variance yardstick is a 3-seed standard deviation of a level, not of the paired difference, measured on a different population at a different operating point, and it is then used to grade three effect sizes.
survived.evidence: §3.9, unchanged: "the generator and filter were retrained under 3 seeds and the whole pipeline re-evaluated on the full test split: macro recall@15 is 0.3437 with a standard deviation of 0.0099, and micro 0.2686 with 0.0058. That study ran on an earlier operating point than the one reported here ... Read against it, the rank fusion of P1 is an order of magnitude larger than retraining noise and the pool cap of P2 several times larger, while the rule budget of P3, at +0.0092 on validation, is within it." The three graded contrasts are measured on the validation draw (n=293) at k=15, not on the full test split, and each is a paired difference whose seed-to-seed spread is not the spread of a level. The paper discloses the operating-point mismatch but not the level-versus-difference one, and 3 seeds is a thin basis for either.
survived.fix: Report the seed-to-seed SD of each registered contrast itself, on the population and operating point that contrast is measured on; or drop the graded verbal comparison and let each prediction's own paired interval carry the argument, since P3's interval already covers zero.

survived.claim: P5's +0.0286 is measured against an unnamed base of 0.5023 rather than the deployed fusion's 0.5353, and the configuration it certifies (0.5308) is below the deployed system on the same population and budget; Table 4's caption calls failed and non-deployed variants deployed choices.
survived.evidence: Confirmed in results/h12_verdict.json, the artifact behind P5: population "n": 291, k 15, micro, with recall_micro["15"] = {"three_way": 0.5308, "two_way": 0.5023} and primary_three_way_minus_two_way gap 0.0286. The deployed fusion on the same 291 substrates at k=15 is 0.5353 (Table 2; \numRankCmpFusionOneFive). So the certified arm is 0.0045 *below* the deployed system, and its base is a configuration named nowhere in the paper -- 0.5023 appears in §3.8 only as the unexplained "interleaved" figure ("block emission being worse than interleaved (0.4376 against 0.5023)"). §3.8 then reports "A binary group ordering entered as the third term reaches 0.5308, the same the trained scorer reaches" without noting it is under the deployed number. Table 4's caption still reads "Every deployed choice as a prediction fixed before it was checked" while listing P6 (-0.1203, of which §3.8 says "That is not the deployed ranking") and P7 (-0.0286), and a third fusion term is absent from the deployed system as described in §2.2 and §2.4.
survived.fix: Name the configuration P5, P6 and P7 are measured against (the two-term fusion at 0.5023, not the deployed 0.5353), state that the three-term arm at 0.5308 sits below the deployed system on the same population and budget, and reword Table 4's caption so it does not describe failed or non-deployed variants as deployed choices.

survived.claim: The SI states a rule for when a ranking comparison carries information and then asserts, as a blanket fact, that the main-text comparison satisfies it, although every comparator's lists are shorter than the budget at k = 30 and 50, the budgets where the lead is claimed.
survived.evidence: SI S10: "a ranking comparison carries information only over the substrates whose pool exceeds the budget, and the number of such substrates should be reported with the result. The comparison in the main text is run on the deployed pool, capped at 100, where the budget is narrower than the pool for every substrate." Section 3.1 says the opposite for the other arms: "at k = 50, 291 of MetaPredictor's lists, 249 of MetaTox's and 282 of the interactive arm's are shorter than the budget." The artifact behind Table 2 (results/deployment_table.json, substrates_whose_list_is_shorter_than_the_budget) records at k = 30: 291 MetaPredictor, 140 MetaTox, 66 SyGMa, 272 GRAIL interactive; and at k = 50 it records 2 for GRAIL exhaustive itself, so the S10 sentence is not even true of the deployed pool. The substantive concession is already made three times (S3.1 "Where a method runs out the budget has stopped measuring ranking"; S4.3 "the advantage at wide budgets is partly a statement about output length on all sides rather than about ranking"; Limitations "the widest columns measure list length on all sides"), which is why this is a scoping defect rather than a claim defect.
survived.fix: Scope the last sentence of S10 to GRAIL's own arm and state its exception ("GRAIL's deployed pool exceeds every budget reported, except for 2 substrates at k = 50"), and add the k = 30 per-arm counts next to the k = 50 counts already in Section 3.1; both sets of counts are already in the pinned artifact.

survived.claim: Table 2 and the SI's ranking-ablation table give different micro recall for what both call the deployed configuration on the same 291 substrates, disagreeing at three of six shared budgets.
survived.evidence: Table 2, GRAIL exh.: 0.4526 (k=10), 0.6391 (k=30), 0.7038 (k=50). SI Table S6 (Table S5 as reviewed), "fusion (deployed)", comparison set n = 291: 0.4496, 0.6406, 0.7068 — while k=1, 5 and 15 are identical in both (0.0902, 0.3098, 0.5353). On 665 references those gaps are +2, -1 and -2 hits, i.e. in both directions, so the parent-drop convention named only in Table 2's caption ("A prediction equal to the substrate is dropped before the budget for every method alike") cannot account for them: dropping the parent can only raise recall at fixed k. The two rows come from different pinned artifacts (results/deployment_table.json vs results/pool_cap_cost.json, cap 100) and neither caption mentions the other or the difference.
survived.fix: Reconcile the two artifacts, or add one sentence to the SI table's caption naming the convention that differs from Table 2 and stating which of the two is the headline configuration. While there, fix the pointers: Section 2.4 and Table 4's footnote send the reader to "Table S5" for the deployed-pool P1 contrast, and Section 3.5 to "Table S3", but in the current SI those are the oracle table and the rule-bank section respectively (the ranking ablation is now S6, the criterion sweep S4).

survived.claim: Section 2.8 states that precision is reported, but no precision figure appears anywhere in the manuscript or the SI.
survived.evidence: Section 2.8: "Precision is reported but is not used to order systems." Every other appearance of the word is qualitative — Section 3.1 "the annotation bias on precision does not explain the difference", Section 4.3 "Precision figures are bounded by annotation completeness", Limitations "Precision is bounded by annotation completeness", SI S6.3 "precision is pessimistic by a bounded but unknown amount, which is why the paper reports it without using it to order systems". Table 2 has no precision column, and paper2/numbers.tex — through which, per S14, "Every number in the paper reaches the page through a macro generated from a pinned artifact" — contains no precision macro at all (0 matches in 621 lines).
survived.fix: Replace "Precision is reported" with what is actually true, e.g. "Precision is computed and released with the per-substrate predictions", or add a precision-at-k column to Table 2 carrying the same annotation-completeness caveat.

survived.claim: Section 3.3 reports five effects and three intervals without naming its evaluation population, in a paper whose stated rule is that no figure is given without one.
survived.evidence: Section 3.3 names no population anywhere: "the learned choice gains +0.4556 at k = 15", "the gain is +0.188 [+0.141, +0.2382]", "the learned choice gains +0.0316 of micro recall at k = 15, [+0.0101, +0.0547], on a base of 0.4481", "at k = 5 the gain is +0.015". The rule it breaks is the paper's own: Section 2.1, "Three evaluation populations appear here... and no figure is given without naming one", and SI S1, "every figure in the paper names one". The adjacent Section 3.4 does comply ("at k = 15 on the comparison set", "+0.2046 on the validation draw"), which makes the omission read as an oversight rather than a convention. The backing artifact settles what it should say: results/selection_ablation_deployed.json records population/source "the comparison set of results/four_method_291.json", n = 291, 665 references, budget 30.
survived.fix: Add "on the comparison set (n = 291, 665 references)" to the first sentence of Section 3.3, and give the base recall for each of the four selection arms alongside their mean pool sizes.

survived.claim: The bank holds templates that compress a multi-enzyme cascade into one rule, so "Predictions are single-step" and the one-step ceiling are not single-step in a chemical sense.
survived.evidence: Section 3.6 concedes the chemistry — "the three sequential 5' phosphorylations that activate it" — and Table 3 shows each reached from the parent by one template: dFdCMP rank 8 rule 2198, dFdCDP rank 21 rule 2139, dFdCTP rank 16 rule 1745. dFdCDP and dFdCTP are two and three kinase steps from gemcitabine, so rules 2139 and 1745 each encode a cascade. This follows from the mining procedure in Section 2.3 ("For each annotated substrate-product pair a ring-aware maximum common substructure is located, the atoms and bonds that changed are flagged as the reaction centre"), which types an annotated parent-metabolite pair however many enzymes separate them. Against that, the Limitations say "Predictions are single-step" and Section 3.11 "Applying the whole bank to every test substrate recovers 0.8171 of references in one step", and nowhere does the text say that "step" means one rule application rather than one enzymatic step. No reported number changes — the ceiling, the depth-two comparison and the recalls are all defined on annotated parent-metabolite pairs — so this is a naming defect, not a measurement one.
survived.fix: Write "one rule application" instead of "single-step" in the Limitations and Section 3.11, and add one sentence to Section 2.3 noting that templates are mined from annotated parent-metabolite pairs and so may compress several enzymatic steps, with the gemcitabine phosphorylations as the instance already in the paper.

survived.claim: The standardisation procedure and the tautomer canonicaliser that defines the default matching criterion are never specified.
survived.evidence: §2.2 gives standardisation only as two citations: "The selected rules are applied with RDKit 2022.09.5, and their products standardised 19,20 and deduplicated." SI Table S2 defines the default key as "canonical tautomer on both sides, then a canonical SMILES without stereochemistry" without naming the canonicaliser; S12 mentions only that the enumerator "lives in a module-level singleton" with a budget of 200. The tanimoto1 row gives "1024-bit Morgan fingerprints" but no radius or chirality flag. Partly overstated — a tool and version (RDKit 2022.09.5) and two standardisation references are on the page — but the canonicaliser's identity and settings, and the Morgan radius, are genuinely absent from a paper titled "under a fully declared evaluation".
survived.fix: Name the tautomer canonicaliser with its scoring/enumeration settings, give the Morgan radius and chirality flag alongside the existing 1024-bit figure, and say in §2.2 which of refs 19–20 the implementation follows (or give the ordered operation list).

survived.claim: The species, matrix, enzyme system and metabolic phase behind the 2,597 reference metabolites are never declared.
survived.evidence: A full-text search of both documents for species/matrix/phase/enzyme terms returns only reference titles and one forward-looking sentence. §2.1 and SI S1 declare sources and versions only: "assembled from four sources: ChEMBL 17, DrugBank 18, MetXBioDB 2 and the GLORYx reference set 4 ... ChEMBL 34, DrugBank 5.1.10, MetXBioDB 1.0 and the GLORYx reference set of 2020." §4.4 then contrasts a future source as "human in vivo data on exactly the population predicted here", which presupposes a characterisation of the present corpus that is nowhere given. In a paper whose stated discipline is that "no figure is given without naming" its population, the biological population is the one that goes unnamed.
survived.fix: Add a census of the 2,597 test references by source and, where the sources record it, by species, matrix (in vivo / in vitro) and biotransformation class (at minimum phase 1 vs phase 2); state explicitly where a source does not record it, and repeat the §3.11 coverage split within that stratification.

survived.claim: The type-invariance claim holds over only two of four tested definitions, and the abstract states it without the qualifier the body applies.
survived.evidence: The abstract is unqualified: "that bound is invariant to how a transformation type is defined, making it a property of the annotation corpus rather than of our implementation." The body qualifies it twice — §3.11: "the bound is invariant to the definition of a type across the whole range in which that definition is meaningful"; Conclusions: "under every definition of a transformation type at which a type still determines a product." Table 5 shows the singleton mass at 87.2%, 73.3%, 8.9%, 2.7% across the four definitions, with "names a transf." yes/yes/no/no — so "every definition" generalises from n = 2, the two adjacent ones already erode by 14 points, and nothing is tested in the 284-to-69 gap where the claimed boundary is supposed to lie.
survived.fix: Carry the body's qualifier into the abstract ("invariant across every definition at which a type still determines a product"), and add at least one intermediate definition between "counts dropped" and "element pairs" so the claimed coincidence of collapse with loss of product-determination is tested rather than assumed.

survived.claim: A template-bank coverage ceiling is claimed to bound sequence-to-sequence predictors, which have no template bank.
survived.evidence: §4.4 states without support or hedge: "The bound applies to any predictor trained on a comparable corpus, including sequence-to-sequence systems, which do not report it." The bound is defined in §3.11 by what the bank reaches — "337 need a transformation type the bank does not hold, 98 need a type it holds whose rule did not fire, and 40 cannot be typed" — and 138 of the 475 are properties of rule firing and typing, not of the corpus at all. A generative model is not restricted to a template vocabulary, and the bank is not purely corpus-derived (§2.3: "the deduplicated union of four curated collections together with templates mined from" train). The measurement is also already in hand: SI S13 records that "MetaTox and MetaPredictor predictions are frozen per substrate and released with the code."
survived.fix: Restrict the sentence to rule-based predictors drawing on a comparable template bank — or measure it, by reporting MetaPredictor's recall on the 475 uncovered references from the frozen per-substrate predictions already released.

survived.claim: The deployed arm's micro recall differs between Table 2 and Table S5 at three shared budgets, and the seeded-permutation baseline differs between §3.2 and §3.4.
survived.evidence: Table 2 gives GRAIL exh. 0.4526, 0.6391, 0.7038 at k = 10, 30, 50; SI Table S5 gives "fusion (deployed)" on the same 291-substrate comparison set as 0.4496, 0.6406, 0.7068. They agree exactly at k = 1, 5 and 15 (0.0902 / 0.3098 / 0.5353) and disagree at the other three. The macros confirm two separate sources: numbers.tex has sweep.bank.10 = 0.4526 while si_table_ranking.tex hardcodes 0.4496. The permutation is the same defect: §3.2 reports "a seeded permutation 0.1128" and §3.4 "A seeded permutation of the same pool reaches 0.1173", from rank.cmp.random15 = 0.1128 and sim.cmp.random15 = 0.1173 (validation: 0.1221 vs 0.1206). Neither document reconciles them, in a paper claiming "every number in this paper comes from one of" 47 pinned artifacts.
survived.fix: Regenerate Table 2 and Table S5 from a single artifact (Table S5 is currently hardcoded rather than macro-driven), or state in the S8 caption which convention differs and why; and declare the seed and arm set behind each permutation control so the two values are distinguishable.

survived.claim: Per-arm coverage - how often each method returns nothing - is conditioned away by the 291-substrate intersection rather than reported, and GRAIL exhaustive's own non-completions are among the failures that define the population.
survived.evidence: The population is an intersection and nothing reports what each arm contributed to it: "The comparison set is the 291 substrates on which every method predicts, carrying 665 references" (Sec. 2.1), and the only qualification is "a quarter of the evaluated test split and not a random quarter of it" (Limitations). The producer confirms the mechanism - scripts/four_method_291.py: `subs = sorted(set(truth) & set.intersection(*(set(p) for p in pools.values())))`. GRAIL exhaustive is one of the failing arms: results/cost_envelope.json records 11 of 106 sampled substrates not finishing at deadline_s 600.0 at the whole bank (about 10%), and that count appears nowhere in the paper - \numEnvelopeUnfinished is defined in numbers.tex but never used in body.tex, which cites only \numEnvelopeSmallestUnfinished. Table 2's last row is mean output length, not coverage.
survived.fix: Add one row to Table 2 giving, for each arm, the number of candidate substrates on which it returned at least one prediction, counting GRAIL exhaustive's 600 s non-completions as failures, and state the deadline in the text rather than only in the Figure 3 legend.

survived.claim: Section 3.1 claims per-arm truncation counts "for every arm" and then gives three of five, omitting the two that bear on the k=50 lead, although the pinned artifact holds all of them at every budget.
survived.evidence:
Current body.tex, unchanged: "Where a method runs out the budget has stopped measuring ranking, and the counts are reported for every arm: at $k=50$, 
umShortMetapredictorFiveZero{} of MetaPredictor's lists, 
umShortMetatoxFiveZero{} of MetaTox's and 
umShortTrainedFiveZero{} of the interactive arm's are shorter than the budget." SyGMa and GRAIL exhaustive are absent, and they are the pair that explains the lead: results/deployment_table.json, key substrates_whose_list_is_shorter_than_the_budget, "50": {'whole bank': 2, 'trained budget': 282, 'metatox': 249, 'sygma': 134, 'metapredictor': 291}. The artifact holds all five arms at all nine budgets, and numbers.tex already carries macros for each (
umShortSygmaFiveZero 134, 
umShortBankFiveZero 2).
survived.fix: Print all five counts at k=50 (bank 2, interactive 282, MetaTox 249, SyGMa 134, MetaPredictor 291) - or delete "for every arm" - and add the full nine-budget, five-arm table to the SI, since deployment_table.json already contains it.

survived.claim: The one head-to-head presented as GRAIL beating MetaTox at matched output rests on a premise its own artifact contradicts, does not name the arm, carries no interval, and reverses sign under the paper's default aggregation.
survived.evidence: Text unchanged: "At a budget of $15$, where MetaTox emits about what the interactive arm emits, its macro recall is 0.5406 against GRAIL's 0.5672. Both emit alike there, so the annotation bias on precision does not explain the difference." The pinned artifact results/h11_grid.json defines the GRAIL arm as `"rule": "the trained rule budget's pool, ordered by the H7 fusion, untruncated"` - i.e. not at a budget of 15 - and records `mean_output: {'rule': 16.31, 'metatox': 36.34}` with `bias_note: "...the rule emits 16.31 against MetaTox's 36.34, so F1 is biased toward the rule..."`. Under the paper's own default aggregation the same pair goes the other way: Table 2 gives GRAIL int. 0.4797 against MetaTox 0.5143 at k=15, and SI Table S3 gives GRAIL interactive minus MetaTox at k=15 as -.035 [-.076, +.006]. The text notes only "That pair is macro; every figure in Table 2 is micro."
survived.fix: Name the arm, state that its 0.5672 is the untruncated interactive pool (mean 16.31) against MetaTox truncated at 15, give the paired interval, and add that under the default micro aggregation the pair reverses to 0.4797 against 0.5143, -0.035 [-0.076, +0.006].

survived.claim: Every verdict cell takes the maximum of two GRAIL arms against the maximum of three comparators and then reads an unadjusted interval, across 45 cells with no multiplicity control.
survived.evidence: Figure 1 caption: "red where GRAIL's better arm trails the strongest comparator with the interval excluding zero, blue where it leads with the interval excluding zero". SI Table S4 caption: "+ marks a budget where GRAIL's better arm leads the strongest comparator with the paired interval excluding zero... Every cell is read from the interval and never from the point estimate" - 5 criteria x 9 budgets = 45 cells. Grepping body.tex and si.tex for holm/multiplicity/Bonferroni returns one hit, and it is the unrelated population analysis in S11 ("none survives a Holm correction"). The family is 54 differences in Table S3, and the abstract's k=30 claim turns on its most marginal cell - the SI itself says "The exhaustive mode's lead over MetaTox at k = 30 excludes zero by little" (+.038 [+.005, +.072]).
survived.fix: State in Sec. 2.8 that the Figure 1 and Table S4 verdicts select the better GRAIL arm and the strongest comparator, and report a multiplicity-controlled verdict over the 54-cell family of Table S3 (Holm, or a max-statistic bootstrap resampling the arm selection with the substrates) beside the unadjusted one, flagging the k=30 lead over MetaTox as the cell that turns on it.

survived.claim: The flat "no training contamination" claim for the 291 rests on a substrate-role audit only; the molecule-role overlap the SI reports for the test split is never reported for the comparison set.
survived.evidence: Main text, unchanged: "The comparison set carries no training contamination: 0 of its 291 substrates appear in train or validation under a canonical key" (Sec. 2.1). The producing audit keys only substrates: scripts/external_overlap_audit.py builds `trained_keys()` from `a[0]` of each train/val triple line - the substrate id - so `seen` is the set of train/val substrates, not of all molecules. The SI reports the other role at split level: "2,408 molecules occur in both train and test, and 243 test substrates appear as molecules in train" (S1) - about 20% of test substrates, a rate the 291 cannot plausibly escape. Section 2.3 then sends the reader to Sec. 2.1 for exactly those counts ("a molecule that is a substrate in training may appear as a product in test; the counts are in Section~\ref{sec:populations}"), where the only figure present is the flat 0.
survived.fix: Report, for the 291, the number occurring anywhere in train or validation as a molecule rather than only in substrate position, and restate the sentence as the role-specific claim the audit supports: no substrate of the comparison set is a training or validation substrate.

survived.claim: Table 2 and the SI stage-ablation table report the same deployed configuration on the same 291 substrates under the same criterion and disagree at three of the six shared budgets, with no reconciliation given.
survived.evidence: Table 2, GRAIL exh.: k=10 0.4526, k=30 0.6391, k=50 0.7038. SI Table S6 (was S5), "fusion (deployed)", comparison set n=291: 0.4496, 0.6406, 0.7068. The other three shared budgets agree exactly (k=1 0.0902, k=5 0.3098, k=15 0.5353), so this is not rounding: the gaps are 2, 1 and 2 references out of 665. The two pinned artifacts differ in a stated convention that no caption mentions - results/four_method_291.json records "parent_and_duplicates": "dropped before the budget is applied" and results/deployment_table.json records "a prediction whose key equals the substrate's is dropped before the budget, for every arm alike", while results/ranking_ablation.json records only "every arm re-ranks one pool built by the deployed configuration" with no parent/duplicate drop. Nor does the parent drop explain the signs: it would make Table 2 higher at every budget, but Table 2 is lower at k=30 and k=50. The Table S6 caption says only "the pool, the matching rule and the budget are fixed", and SI S9.1 shows the authors already track one-reference effects of this size ("moves micro recall at k=1 from 0.1053 to 0.1068, a difference of 0.0015") without connecting them to this discrepancy. In a paper that claims "Every number in the paper reaches the page through a macro generated from a pinned artifact", two pinned artifacts disagreeing about the flagship configuration is the failure the provenance machinery is advertised to prevent.

survived.evidence: Table 2 caption: "A prediction equal to the substrate is dropped before the budget for every method alike." survived.claim: §3.6 calls the mined portion "the half of the bank with no expert provenance" when the paper's own counts make it about three quarters.

survived.fix: In §3.6 replace "the half of the bank with no expert provenance is the half carrying this molecule" with the measured share (about three quarters), and drop or qualify the "two halves" phrasing in SI §S5 where it is immediately followed by 1,725 against 5,856.

survived.claim: §3.8's "a third of the headroom" does not follow from the two numbers printed with it.

survived.fix: Change the sentence to name what replicates — the fusion separating from each single scorer and from their product — rather than "the same ordering of arms", so the qualification that follows is a detail and not a reversal.

survived.claim: §2.4's +0.109 is reported without naming its population, against the paper's own rule in §2.1.
survived.evidence: §2.1 declares exactly three populations and the rule: "Three evaluation populations appear here, each a stated subset of a split rather than a split itself, and no figure is given without naming one" — the evaluated test set, the validation draw, and the comparison set. §2.4 then reads: "On the set where the variant was chosen among four it gives +0.109, and the shrinkage to two thirds is the measured cost of that selection." The selection set is described only by what was done on it and matches none of the three by name. The neighbouring sentence shows the paper knows how to do this: "On the pool the deployed system actually ranks the same contrast, same population and same budget, is +0.0519". +0.109 is also the one figure in this passage hardcoded in body.tex rather than reaching the page through a numbers.tex macro.
survived.fix: Name the selection population and its size in §2.4, and if it is not one of the three, add it to the declared list in §2.1 so the rule stated there still holds.

survived.claim: §4.3's "A reader therefore cannot presently verify any ranking in this literature" is a universal claim the paper's own Table 2 and availability statement contradict.
survived.evidence: §4.3: "Of 4 such systems, one releases training code without a checkpoint, one has a withdrawn module, one offers only a web form and one has no repository. A reader therefore cannot presently verify any ranking in this literature". One page earlier, §4.2 claims the opposite for this paper's own comparison: "every evaluation choice is declared with every cell of the resulting grid reported, which is what makes the comparison reproducible by a third party", and §7 releases "the frozen per-substrate predictions of every comparator, the evaluation harness". Table 2 is a ranking in this literature (GRAIL, MetaTox, SyGMa, MetaPredictor at nine budgets) and is, by the paper's own account, verifiable.
survived.fix: Restrict the sentence to the systems it follows from — e.g. "A reader therefore cannot presently verify any ranking involving the 2025-26 wave" — leaving the case for per-item predictions intact.

survived.claim: The "twenty configurations" offered as evidence that P5's +0.0286 is not a selection artefact appear in no table of the paper or the SI.
survived.evidence: Current §3.8 still reads: "P5 used the same model untrained further, entering its group score as a third ranking in the same fusion. Measured +0.0286, 95% CI [+0.0085, +0.0502]. The effect is not selection: all twenty configurations beat the base on validation and 70% of that margin survived the move." The current SI runs S1-S14 with Tables S1-S7 (splits, criteria, intervals, criterion sweep, oracle, ranking ablation, worked example); a grep for "configuration" across si.pdf returns only "the released configuration", "the deployed configuration" and the S9 heading. Neither the twenty configurations, their validation values, nor a definition of what a "configuration" is appears anywhere, and "70% of that margin" is not derivable from any released table in the two documents.
survived.fix: Either add a short SI table listing the twenty configurations with their validation values and the base (which makes both "all twenty" and "70%" checkable), or delete the sentence and let P5 stand on its measured +0.0286 [+0.0085, +0.0502].

survived.claim: The paper analyses the corpus licences in detail but states no licence for its own code, its rule bank, or the third-party comparator predictions it redistributes.
survived.evidence: §7 as it now stands: "Source code, the split manifest, the frozen per-substrate predictions of every comparator, the evaluation harness, the provenance sweep and the preregistration with every hypothesis and its outcome are at github.com/doctawho42/GRAIL" - no licence is named for any of it. SI §S14: "MetaTox and MetaPredictor predictions are frozen per substrate and released with the code", again with no terms, while the same SI devotes a page to ChEMBL's CC BY-SA 3.0, DrugBank's CC BY-NC 4.0 and BioTransformer's redistribution clause. The rule bank is now flagged but still unlicensed: SI §S5 says "The published source of each collection, and the licence each carries, is [CURATED RULES: the published source, if any, of each of the four curated collections, and the licence each carries]; a reader should treat the curated half as unattributed until it is."
survived.fix: Name a licence for the released code and for the rule bank in §7, and add one sentence to §S14 on the terms under which the frozen MetaTox and MetaPredictor predictions are redistributed.

survived.claim: The GLORYx citation pairs year 2020 with volume 34 (a 2021 volume), and that citation doubles as the version identifier for one of the four corpus sources.
survived.evidence: Reference 4 and SI reference S4 both still read "GLORYx: Prediction of the Metabolites Resulting from Phase 1 and Phase 2 Biotransformations of Xenobiotics. Toxicol. 2021, 34 (2) (DOI 10.1021/acs.chemrestox.0c00224, which paper2/refs.bib records as year={2020}, volume={34}, number={2}). The same "2020" is load-bearing as a version string: §2.1 and §7 say "the GLORYx reference set of 2020", and SI §S1 repeats "MetXBioDB 1.0 and the GLORYx reference set of 2020" - so a reader is asked to identify one of the four corpus sources by a year that does not match the cited volume.
survived.fix: Cite the issue version (Chem. Res. Toxicol. 2021, 34, 286-299) in both reference lists, and identify the GLORYx reference set by its distributed file, release or DOI rather than by a year.

survived.claim: The k=15 MetaTox paragraph asserts that MetaTox and the interactive arm "emit alike" against a table on the same page showing 30.9 vs 15.6, and never says which GRAIL arm 0.5672 belongs to.
survived.evidence: §3.1 is unchanged: "At a budget of 15, where MetaTox emits about what the interactive arm emits, its macro recall is 0.5406 against GRAIL's 0.5672. Both emit alike there, so the annotation bias on precision does not explain the difference." Table 2 on the same page ends "list | 98.1 | 15.6 | 30.9 | 40.5 | 10.7", i.e. MetaTox emits twice the interactive arm; nothing in the text says the premise concerns lengths after truncation at k=15. survived.fix: Name the arm ("GRAIL's interactive arm, 0.5672") and give the two mean emitted-list lengths that the "emit alike" claim rests on - the interactive arm's 16.31 against MetaTox truncated at 15 - so the sentence can be reconciled with Table 2's list row.

survived.claim: Figure 3's right panel sets four statistics of the interactive mode beside one of the exhaustive mode, uses a third colour for the slowest bar with nothing explaining it, and carries no legend or note that the exhaustive mean and tail do not exist.

The interactive mode's mean is six times its median and its slowest substrate is three orders above it." survived.fix: Draw "did not finish" markers at the exhaustive mode's mean, 90th percentile and slowest positions so both modes carry the same four statistics, and add a one-line note to the caption saying the orange bar is the interactive tail and not a timeout.

survived.claim: Figure 2's right panel uses a non-uniformly spaced rank axis without declaring it, and beyond ~rank 55 the exhaustive arm's ticks merge into a solid grey block, so the caption's "every returned candidate drawn as a tick" cannot be read.
survived.evidence: The caption is silent on the scale: "Right: where the four annotated metabolites fall in each arm's ranked list, every returned candidate drawn as a tick. The interactive budget never produces the phosphorylations, so its list is short and correct rather than long and wrong." The axis carries only bare labels "1 5 10 15 20 30 50 100" over "rank in the returned list", which is a symlog scale (linear to 30, logarithmic beyond). In the rendered fig_case.pdf the exhaustive row's ticks become contiguous from roughly rank 45 onward — at that spacing the gap between consecutive ranks falls below the 0.8 pt tick line width — and render as one uninterrupted grey band out to 100. The SI does not recover it: Table S6 gives only "The first twenty of the 100 candidates the exhaustive mode returns", with "The complete ranked lists of both modes ... in the released artifacts."
survived.fix: Add one clause to the caption stating the scale (e.g. "the rank axis is linear to 30 and logarithmic beyond"), and either thin the ticks or label the compressed region with its count so the band beyond k=30 is read as a count rather than as individual candidates.
